latestVersion.changelog: Methodology upgrade, not just wording. R1 objections now require a verifiable anchor (file:line, runnable command, citable data) plus a mandatory closing question: what's the failure scenario for NOT acting. R2 rulings carry an evidence tag - verified / reasoned / to-verify - and only verified items are consensus-eligible. R3 no longer forces a consensus list: it outputs three categories (still disputed / unresolved-no-evidence-either-side / verified consensus), and failing to converge is not treated as a failure. R4 fresh judge is now mandatory whenever a trigger fires (a prohibition in the consensus, zero rejections all session, or 5+ consensus items) instead of optional. Core stances gained a hard number: across an archived sample, only ~1 in 40 objections was actually rejected, and every real rejection came from running production data - a warning against mistaking agreement for a working debate. New closing-handoff step: standalone use has no outer process to catch the consensus, so the session must propose where each verified item lands and wait for confirmation, flagging anything unconfirmed rather than dropping it silently. Also fixed: a shell-quoting pitfall where a prompt containing backticks breaks command substitution unless piped through a heredoc first.
